Legal

Privacy Notice

How information is handled across the website, inquiries, and the planned Atomic service.

Draft version 0.1 · Prepared 19 October 2026

On this page1. Who this notice covers2. The current website3. Information and purposes4. Legal bases5. AI processing and training6. Recipients and international transfers7. Retention and deletion8. Your choices and rights9. Children, automation, and updates
Draft for review · Not yet effectivePrepared 19 October 2026. This is proposed wording for Atomic’s launch, not an effective agreement or a completed compliance statement. Items marked “To finalize” require company verification and legal review before activation.

1. Who this notice covers

Atomic is a product by Abstract Machines. This notice is intended to cover the Atomic marketing website, inquiries, account administration, billing, and use of the app-building service. Contact the Atomic team at info@absmach.eu with a privacy question.

To finalize: identify the full legal name, registered address, company registration details, controller establishment, applicable representatives, and any appointed data protection officer. “Abstract Machines” is currently a brand reference, not a verified contracting entity.

2. The current website

The current website offers interactive demonstrations using sample data. Booking requests, shopping bags, and project selections exist in page memory and reset when the page reloads. They are not sent to a booking, payment, or generation backend by this site’s application code.

When you enter an idea, the site prepares an email draft locally. Clicking the email link opens your email application. The message reaches the team only if you send it. Your email provider and the team’s email provider then handle the message through their services. Hosting may separately process request metadata such as IP addresses and access logs.

3. Information and purposes

For inquiries, the team receives information you choose to send, such as your name, email address, idea, and correspondence. That information is used to respond and discuss access. Avoid including unnecessary personal data or confidential production records.

The planned service may process account identifiers, workspace membership, prompts, code, uploaded files, support correspondence, usage events, and billing records to provide and administer the service. Customer apps may contain personal data processed on the customer’s instructions under a DPA.

To finalize: verify the actual account, telemetry, billing, and support data fields and purposes; distinguish mandatory from optional information and explain the consequences of not providing required fields.

4. Legal bases

The proposed bases, where applicable law requires a legal basis, are steps taken at your request before entering a contract and performance of that contract; legitimate interests in responding to inquiries, operating and securing the service, and preventing abuse; legal obligations for required records; and consent for activities that require it.

To finalize: map each actual purpose to an appropriate basis and document any legitimate-interest assessment. An inquiry must not automatically enroll someone in unrelated marketing. Where processing relies on consent, it may be withdrawn without affecting prior lawful processing.

5. AI processing and training

Delivering AI-assisted building may require sending selected prompts, source context, or files to model providers. The exact providers, data sent, locations, retention, and contractual training restrictions must be disclosed before production use.

To finalize: approve Atomic’s own training and product-improvement policy and verify each provider’s terms and settings. This draft does not promise that all providers offer zero retention or exclude all data from training. Do not interpret it as permission for unrestricted reuse of customer content.

6. Recipients and international transfers

Depending on the deployed service, recipients may include hosting, AI inference, email, support, and payment providers, authorized personnel, professional advisers, and authorities where disclosure is legally required. Customer-directed integrations may have separate terms.

To finalize: identify actual recipients and their roles, update the subprocessor register, and document processing locations. Where international-transfer rules apply, identify the relevant adequacy decision or safeguards, such as properly completed Standard Contractual Clauses and any necessary supplementary measures. Explain how to obtain a copy of those safeguards.

7. Retention and deletion

Information should be retained only as needed for its stated purpose, applicable recordkeeping obligations, and legitimate dispute or security needs. Customer app data must follow the agreed DPA and service retention schedule.

To finalize: set concrete retention periods or meaningful criteria for inquiries, accounts, prompts, build logs, billing records, abuse records, and backups; define deletion timing and any account-closure export window. The current local demonstrations reset on reload; this says nothing about hosting logs or sent emails.

8. Your choices and rights

Depending on the law that applies, you may have rights to access, correct, erase, restrict, or receive a portable copy of personal data, and to object to certain processing, including direct marketing. You may also complain to a competent data protection authority. These rights have legal conditions and exceptions.

Send a request to the contact above. The team may need proportionate information to verify your identity. If your information belongs to an app built by another customer, contact that app’s operator; Atomic’s role may be to assist that operator as a processor.

To finalize: identify applicable supervisory authorities, request-handling deadlines and procedures, and any additional regional rights.

9. Children, automation, and updates

The proposed builder service is intended for adults and authorized business users. Any support for minors requires a separately reviewed approach. AI-generated code is not itself a determination of an individual’s legal rights.

To finalize: verify age restrictions and whether any operational automated decisions have legal or similarly significant effects. Disclose the required details if they do. Publish an effective date and communicate material changes when this notice is finalized.
